newsitem.title: USA: New York schools ordered to study Irish famine.
newsitem.headline: New York schools ordered to study Irish famine.

text.p: New York Gov. George Pataki honoured Irish President Mary Robinson on Wednesday by signing a new law that will make the Irish potato famine a required lesson in New York public schools.
The law makes New York the first state in the nation to order schools to devote attention to the mass starvation in Ireland in the mid-19th century, officials said.

"History teaches us the Great Irish Hunger was not the result of massive failure of the Irish potato crop but rather was the result of a deliberate campaign by the British to deny the Irish people the food they needed to survive," Pataki said at a breakfast honouring Robinson.

Pataki held the event to honour Robinson for being "at the forefront of trade links between New York and Ireland," said a spokeswoman for the governor. The governor's grandmother came from County Louth, which is Robinson's home, she added.

The new law adds the study of famine to an existing law that requires the state Board of Regents to establish classes to study patriotism, citizenship and human rights, including genocide, slavery and the Holocaust.
Opponents complained that the new law panders to the Irish vote in New York, a stronghold of Irish immigrants.
